scripts.prebuild: pnpm verify:env && pnpm generate:types && pnpm generate:importmap && next typegen
scripts.build: pnpm verify:env && pnpm generate:importmap && next build

comments.exactPins: next, react, react-dom and every @payloadcms/* package are pinned exactly. @payloadcms/next@3.88.0 accepts only next '>=15.2.9 <15.3.0 || >=15.3.9 <15.4.0 || >=15.4.11 <15.5.0 || >=16.2.6 <17.0.0'. Re-check with `npm view @payloadcms/next@<v> peerDependencies` before any upgrade.
comments.graphql: Pinned to 16.x deliberately. Payload's peer range is ^16.8.1 — graphql 17 is published as latest and WILL break the install.
comments.typescript: Pinned to 5.9.3. TypeScript 7 (the native port) is published as latest, but typescript-eslint declares `typescript: '>=4.8.4 <6.1.0'` — TS 7 breaks linting outright, quite apart from being unvalidated against Payload.
comments.eslint: ESLint 9 with flat config. ESLint 10 is published and typescript-eslint supports it, but 9 is the battle-tested choice for a new project. @eslint/js is a SEPARATE package in flat config — it does not ship with eslint.
comments.bundler: Next 16 uses Turbopack for dev and build by default. If the Phase 0 spike (plan 3.1c) shows Payload failing under a Turbopack production build, change `build` to `next build --webpack` and record it in docs/DECISIONS.md.
comments.lint: `next lint` was removed in Next 16 and `next build` no longer lints. ESLint runs as its own script and its own CI step.
comments.migrations: Payload 3.88 migrate:create emits MigrateUpArgs/MigrateDownArgs as a VALUE import, but db-postgres exports them as types only — the migration then throws at runtime under ESM. The repair is CHAINED into migrate:create, not wired as a post- script, because pnpm does not run pre/post scripts by default (v7+). Always create migrations with 'pnpm migrate:create'; calling 'pnpm payload migrate:create' directly skips the repair.
comments.buildCodegen: generate:importmap is CHAINED into `build` for the same reason as migrations above: pnpm does not run pre/post scripts (v7+), so the `prebuild` hook never fires under 'pnpm run build' — which is exactly what Vercel runs. importMap.js is gitignored (**/importMap.js), so a fresh deploy checkout had no copy and the build failed with "Can't resolve '../importMap.js'". Generating it is preferred to committing it: it is derived from payload.config.ts and a committed copy goes stale silently. prebuild is left in place for npm, where it also runs verify:env and generate:types.
